Hi Maya,

Thanks again for yesterday's call — really helpful to understand Redwood's routing and caching capabilities. We walked away thinking a technical deep-dive (60-90m) with our infra and ML engineers would be the right next step so we can validate performance assumptions and integration points.

High-level ask: can we lock a 60–90 minute session in the next two weeks that includes someone from your runtime/serving team and your SE to go through:
- model variants & quantization tradeoffs
- batching / KV cache behavior under mixed traffic
- deployment options (hosted vs private) and network implications

Our initial availability: Tue Jul 22 (10–12 PT), Thu Jul 24 (14–17 PT), or Mon Jul 28 (all day PT).

Attendees from our side will be: myself (Platform PM), Arjun Kumar (Infra Lead), and Priya Shah (ML Ops).

Can you propose an agenda and confirm who from Redwood would join? Also, could you share any pre-read or runbook so our infra team can prepare telemetry/benchmarks they'd like to see?

Thanks,
Lisa Park
Senior PM, Integrations — Orion Health
lisa.park@orionhealth.com

Hi Lisa — great to hear. Glad the discovery helped.

We can absolutely run a 60–90min technical deep-dive focused on the items you listed. Proposed slots based on your availability:
- Tue 22 Jul 10:30–11:45 PT (75m)
- Thu 24 Jul 14:00–15:30 PT (90m)
- Mon 28 Jul 09:00–10:15 PT (75m)

Suggested agenda (we'll refine once attendees are confirmed):
1) 10m — goal alignment & success criteria (you)
2) 25m — runtime architecture & routing policies (Connor)
3) 25m — demo of batching/KV cache effects on latency & cost (Ben)
4) 20–30m — integration considerations: VPC, auth, and telemetry (Maya + Ben)
5) 10–15m — Q&A / next steps / action items

I've attached a short runbook/agenda v1 for your team to review — it includes the telemetry samples we typically request. If that looks good, we'll lock one of the slots and invite Connor (runtime owner) for architecture questions.

One ask from our side: can you confirm whether the session should include exec-level stakeholders, or keep it to engineering/infra folks? That helps set pace and depth.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai

Adding Connor as runtime owner — he'll lead the architecture portion. A couple of prep notes we should share with the customer so their infra team can bring useful artifacts:
- sample request distribution (seq lengths, tokens per call) or a small workload trace (1–2 hours)
- current latency / p50-p99 numbers and cost targets
- any firewall/NAT restrictions or peering constraints for private deployment

Connor — for the agenda above, would you be comfortable covering kernel/compilation choices at a high level and the fallback routing policy? We should leave 10 minutes for a short profiling demo showing how prefix caching reduces token throughput during steady state.

I'll prepare a short slide deck and the profiling notebook to run during the call. Linking the internal prep doc here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-tdx-prep
